subject: Inference landscape & QBR playbook — pricing alerts + model-release tracking
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah Morgan <leah@rivet.ai>, ops-research@compass.ai
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Inference landscape & QBR playbook — pricing alerts + model-release tracking

Team — sharing a concise snapshot ahead of the QBR prep block next week. This is intended to be the leadership-level appendix to the QBR slide deck and the one-pager we share with sales/CS. Key points below; marked asks at the end. Attachment: 20261128-market-clipboard.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Market moves (last 7 days):
- Rivet Analytics announced a new 7B quantized variant (Rivet-Light-7b) with aggressive per-token pricing (roughly 30–40% below typical hosted list for similar throughput).
- CompassAI pushed a new managed endpoint SKU with guaranteed 95ms p50 for short sequences (marketing says “predictable latency” — we should validate).
- Open-source: two groups released smaller architecture tweaks that improve decoding speed on recent kernels (could affect inference cost baselines).

Implications for our QBR narrative:
- Pricing: call out where we hold value (dedicated predictable throughput, private deployments, cost levers) but acknowledge the short-term competitive price pressure.
- Model releases: competitors are shipping smaller, cheaper flavors — highlight our runtime + compile optimizations and quantization profiles as the differentiator.
- Positioning: pivot from "cheapest" to "predictable economics + operational resilience" for enterprise deals.

Asks:
1) Lauren — can you add a cost-delta table (per 1M tokens) vs Rivet-Light-7b and CompassAI short-seq SKU into the attached spreadsheet? Put rows for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
2) Markus — draft 2 slide bullets for the QBR exec summary that emphasize what we control (routing, caching, SLAs).
3) Leah/Ops — if you have any validated benchmark links, paste them in the sheet.

I'll consolidate inputs by Monday EOD and push the deck to the docs link.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Field Strategy | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

On Sat, Nov 28, 2026 at 09:12, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — sharing a concise snapshot ahead of the QBR prep block next week. ...

Thanks Jordan — added a quick worksheet to the spreadsheet with candidate price deltas and assumptions (see tab "Lauren-cost-deltas"). High-level notes:
- Rivet-Light-7b pricing looks attractive for low-concurrency workloads; it assumes 8-bit quantization and heavy batching. For customers with strict latency needs, their claims look aspirational unless routing/batching is handled client-side.
- CompassAI short-seq SKU will help them on p50 for 8–32 tokens, but their p95/99 signals look worse.

I want procurement to see the "what we lose" and "what we win" side-by-side. I pasted the HubSpot opportunity link below for OPP-2345; it contains customer-specific usage patterns we should call out.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/2345

I've attached a short CSV export (copied into the spreadsheet) with sample token distributions from three named accounts. Use that under the "customer impact" slide.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Inference landscape & QBR playbook — pricing alerts + model-release tracking

Jordan / Lauren — good capture. I drafted two executive bullets and a short "talking points" section; added as a PDF slide draft (qbr-slide-draft.pdf). Toplines:
- Executive bullets (for CEO slide):
  1) Market: New low-cost, small-parameter offerings are compressing price comps — we expect short-term RFQs from price-sensitive buyers.
  2) Our levers: throughput SLAs, predictable unit economics (Dedicated), private deployment compliance, and integrated optimization suite (Optimize) deliver superior enterprise TCO in targeted workloads.

- Recommended framing for the field: Lead with risk (latency/regression) and TCO (beyond headline token price). Use two customer examples from the spreadsheet to show when Rivet-Light is cheaper and when our Dedicated/private stack is 20–40% lower total cost due to batching/caching and fewer tail retries.

- Small note on model releases: Rivet's 7b announcement includes a tradeoff (reduced context window and no KV-cache optimization yet). We should validate their claimed throughput with the Bench team before we treat it as a direct competitor.

Attaching: qbr-slide-draft.pdf (one slide with bullets + suggested chart).

—Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Product — Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
